scenes.heading: Metabolism and enzymes
scenes.sub: How cells power and speed up their reactions
scenes.say: Thousands of reactions happen every second in each of your cells. Most would be far too slow without enzymes, and many need energy from ATP.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A power bank charges a phone that can't run by itself
scenes.science: ATP drives endergonic reactions by energy coupling
scenes.breaks: ATP doesn't send energy down a cable: it usually hands a phosphate to the reactant, and the products are far more stable.
scenes.say: Think of ATP as a phone power bank. An endergonic reaction is a flat phone that can't run by itself. Plug in ATP, and the job happens. Once used, ATP is flat as A D P plus phosphate, and respiration recharges it.

scenes.heading: Free energy
scenes.say: Ex means exit, en means enter. In exergonic reactions, delta G is negative: free energy exits and the reaction is spontaneous. But spontaneous doesn't mean fast. In endergonic reactions, delta G is positive, so energy must go in.
scenes.caption: Ex means exit, en means enter. In exergonic reactions, ΔG is negative: free energy exits and the reaction is spontaneous. But spontaneous doesn't mean fast. In endergonic reactions, ΔG is positive, so energy must go in.

scenes.heading: Energy coupling
scenes.question: Glutamine synthesis has ΔG°′ = +14.2 kJ mol⁻¹. ATP hydrolysis is −30.5. Can the coupled reaction go?
lines: Add the ΔG values with their signs
Negative, so the coupled reaction can go
scenes.say: Making glutamine has a delta G of plus fourteen point two kilojoules per mole. ATP hydrolysis is minus thirty point five. Just add them with their signs: minus sixteen point three. It's negative, so the coupled reaction can go.
scenes.caption: Making glutamine has ΔG of +14.2 kJ mol⁻¹. ATP hydrolysis is −30.5. Just add them with their signs: −16.3 kJ mol⁻¹. It's negative, so the coupled reaction can go.

scenes.heading: How enzymes work
points: Do NOT change ΔG or equilibrium
Induced fit at the active site
Denature above optimum temperature or pH
scenes.say: Enzymes dig a tunnel through the hill, but don't move the valleys. They lower the activation energy, but delta G and the equilibrium stay the same. The active site shifts to grip the substrate: induced fit. Too hot, or the wrong pH, and the enzyme denatures.
scenes.caption: Enzymes dig a tunnel through the hill, but don't move the valleys. They lower the activation energy, but ΔG and the equilibrium stay the same. The active site shifts to grip the substrate: induced fit. Too hot, or the wrong pH, and the enzyme denatures.

scenes.heading: Michaelis–Menten
scenes.say: Like a canteen at lunch, once all staff are busy, the enzyme is saturated at V max. K m is the half-way house: the substrate concentration where the rate is half of V max. A low K m means high affinity.
scenes.caption: Like a canteen at lunch, once all staff are busy, the enzyme is saturated at Vmax. Km is the half-way house: the [S] where the rate is half of Vmax. A low Km means high affinity.

scenes.heading: Types of inhibitor
scenes.say: Compete, K m climbs. Non-compete, the max gets beat. A competitive inhibitor blocks the active site, but flooding with substrate still reaches V max. A non-competitive inhibitor binds elsewhere and lowers V max. In feedback inhibition, an end product switches off an early enzyme.

points: ATP couples to drive endergonic reactions
Km = [S] at ½Vmax; low Km = high affinity
Competitive: Km up; non-competitive: Vmax down
scenes.say: Quick recap. Negative delta G is spontaneous. ATP drives endergonic reactions. Enzymes lower activation energy, not delta G. K m is the half-way house. Competitive inhibitors raise K m, non-competitive inhibitors lower V max. Now try the practice questions!
